verses.text: Job continued speaking:
"How I long for the months that have passed, for the days when God watched over me,
when his lamp shone over my head, and by his light I walked through the darkness!
Those were the best days of my life, when God's friendship blessed my home,
when the Almighty was still with me and my children were all around me,
when my path was rich with cream, and the rocks poured out streams of olive oil for me.
When I went to the city gate and took my seat in the public square,
the young men saw me and stepped aside, and the old men stood up out of respect.
The leaders stopped talking and covered their mouths with their hands.
The voices of the important men became quiet, and their tongues stuck to the roofs of their mouths.
Everyone who heard me spoke well of me, and everyone who saw me praised me,
because I rescued the poor who cried for help, and the orphans who had no one to help them.
People who were dying blessed me, and I made widows' hearts sing for joy.
I wore goodness like clothing. Justice was my robe and my turban.
I was eyes for the blind and feet for those who could not walk.
I was a father to the needy, and I took up the case of strangers.
I broke the teeth of evil people and snatched their victims from their mouths.
I thought, 'I will die in my own home, after a life with days as many as the grains of sand.
My roots will reach down to the water, and the dew will lie on my branches all night.
I will always be honored, and my strength will always be new, like a bow that never weakens.'
People listened to me and waited quietly for my advice.
After I spoke, they had nothing more to say. My words fell gently on their ears.
They waited for me as people wait for rain. They drank in my words like spring rain.
When they were discouraged, I smiled at them, and my cheerful face encouraged them.
I chose the way for them and sat as their leader. I lived like a king among his troops, like someone who comforts those who mourn.
